title: Charcuterie Board for 10
summary: A board for ten to serve as the main event. Allow 150-200 g of food per person, with roughly as much cheese as meat.

items.note: hard (Parmesan, Pecorino), semi-soft (Gouda, Cheddar), soft (Brie, goat's cheese) and blue
such as baguette, ciabatta or focaccia
such as hummus, pesto or olive tapenade
such as grapes, figs or dried apricots

steps.text: Start with the cheeses, a mix of hard, semi-soft, soft and blue. Arrange them on the board in clusters rather than rows.
Add the charcuterie in clusters of its own, keeping the amount of meat close to the amount of cheese.
Fill in around them with the crackers, breadsticks and bread, then the dip, olives, pickled vegetables, fresh fruit, and nuts and dried fruit.
Finish with the honey or fruit preserves and the mustards.

tips: Dips add variety and help stretch the portions. When the board is the main event, 150-200 g per person ensures guests leave satisfied. Arrange everything in clusters rather than rows for visual appeal. All the amounts are a guide: change them to suit your guests and what you can find.
